reply_text:
*I’d hold the merge.* Reviewed `http-retries` (`b04b610`) against `main` (`5f9be03`). Three findings:

1. *High — `timeoutMs: 0` no longer disables timeouts* — `src/http.js:11`
   Changing `??` to `||` replaces zero with the 10-second default. `src/export.js:4` explicitly uses zero for long-running exports, so requests taking over ten seconds before returning a response will now abort. Confirmed: main schedules no timer; this branch schedules 10,000 ms. Restore nullish defaulting and add a zero-timeout regression test.

2. *High — automatic retries can duplicate non-idempotent operations* — `src/http.js:30–33`
   Retries apply to every method, including POST, without opt-in or an idempotency safeguard. A server can commit a write and still return 503; replaying it can repeat the side effect. An inline reproduction produced three POST side effects from one `request()` call. Default retries should be restricted to safely replayable requests, with explicit opt-in for others.

3. *Medium — discarded retry responses aren’t drained or cancelled* — `src/http.js:31–33`
   On a retryable response, the loop abandons its body before issuing another request. With real fetch responses, unread bodies can retain connections/resources and exhaust connection pools under sustained failures. Confirmed neither consumption nor cancellation occurs for the discarded responses. Release each response body before retrying.

*Validation:* All three existing tests pass, but they don’t cover these cases. I also ran read-only, inline checks for the findings above. No files changed.
